title: Rent vs. revenue
summary: Check whether the rent is reasonable for what you sell.

what: Rent is one of the heaviest fixed costs. As a rule of thumb, it shouldn't exceed 10% of net revenue, and around 5% is optimal.
It's worth projecting sales before signing, to know whether the rent of the space you like is within those limits.

variables.name: Rent
variables.description: What you pay each month for the premises.

steps: Divide the rent by the net revenue and multiply by 100.

examples.title: The café's rent
paragraphs: With $60,000 of rent and $1,107,897.50 of net sales, rent is 5.42% of revenue: acceptable, just above the optimum.
For it to be 5%, net monthly sales would have to reach $1,200,000.

notes.text: If the space is bigger than you need, try to negotiate the rent in proportion to the meters you'll actually use.
